content: 1. Communityor home-based directly observed therapy (DOT) is recommended over health facility-based DOT or unsupervised treatment. This recommendation is conditional and based on moderate certainty in the evidence. 2. DOT administered by trained lay providers or healthcare workers is preferred over DOT administered by family members or unsupervised treatment. This recommendation is conditional and based on very low certainty in the evidence. 3. Video-observed treatment (VOT) may be used as a substitute for in-person DOT when video communication technology is available and can be effectively organized and operated by healthcare providers and patients. This recommendation is conditional and based on very low certainty in the evidence. 4. Patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) should primarily receive ambulatory care rather than care models that rely heavily on hospitalization. This recommendation is conditional and based on very low-quality evidence. 5. A decentralized model of care is recommended over a centralized model for patients undergoing MDR-TB treatment. This recommendation is conditional and based on very low certainty in the evidence. 6. Tracers, such as home visits, SMS messages, or telephone calls, are used to maintain communication with patients and support adherence to treatment. 7. Digital medication monitors, which track the time between openings of a pillbox, can provide audio reminders or send SMS notifications to remind patients to take their medications. These devices also record when the pillbox is opened. 8. Material support, such as food, financial assistance, transportation subsidies, or housing incentives, can help address the indirect costs incurred by patients or their caregivers in accessing healthcare services. This support may also mitigate the consequences of income loss related to the disease. 9. Psychological support, including counseling sessions or peer-group support, is an important component of care. 10. Staff education initiatives, such as adherence education, visual reminders, decision-making tools, and desktop aids, can improve treatment outcomes. 11. Treatment adherence is defined as taking more than 90% of prescribed medications under direct observation by another person. 12. DOT can be administered by healthcare workers, trained lay providers, or family members, and it can take place at home, in the community, or at a clinic. DOT is generally administered daily. 13. When comparing DOT to self-administered therapy (SAT), patients on DOT generally have better treatment success rates, adherence, and two-month sputum conversion rates. They also experience slightly lower rates of loss to follow-up and acquired drug resistance. However, relapse rates may be slightly higher with DOT. 14. DOT provided by healthcare workers or trained lay providers is preferred over DOT provided by family members. Family member-provided DOT is the least preferred option due to higher rates of mortality, loss to follow-up, and treatment failure. 15. Communityor home-based DOT is preferred over health facility-based DOT and SAT. Communityor home-based DOT is associated with higher rates of treatment success, cure, and adherence, as well as lower rates of mortality and unfavorable outcomes. 16. VOT offers the potential to observe treatment adherence remotely, even when patients travel or cannot visit a DOT provider. It is more flexible for patients' schedules and can reduce costs and inconvenience compared to in-person DOT. 17. VOT can be used as an addition to or interchangeably with in-person DOT or other treatment administration options. It is not expected to be the sole supervision method for the entire treatment duration. 18. The technology required for VOT, such as broadband internet and smartphones, is becoming increasingly available in resource-constrained settings. This may enhance real-time communication and improve treatment adherence. 19. Evidence and best practices for VOT are likely to evolve as ongoing randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and programmatic experiences provide further insights. 20. The benefits of VOT may become more apparent as programs integrate it into their care models and as technology becomes more accessible.
